summary.headline: ERP Platform demonstrates high ledger integrity, robust tenant isolation, and strict Calm Ledger UX standards; git history secret rotation is required for production readiness.
summary.grade_note: Core financial ledger, stock movements, and access controls are solid (all 236 unit tests passing, zero lint and type errors). Overall grade is capped at D due to historical commit f58a6b1a containing secrets in git history; rotating credentials elevates the grade to B.

top_risks.text: Historical commit f58a6b1a contains JWT_SECRET and NEXTAUTH_SECRET in git history.
Public login route lacks application-layer rate limiting against automated credential brute-forcing.
Full-history General Ledger reports load all records into memory without streaming.

do_this_week: Rotate JWT_SECRET, NEXTAUTH_SECRET, and database passwords on any live deployment environments.
Add composite index @@index([companyId, status, voucherDate(sort: Desc)]) on vouchers table.

fix_first.reason: Secret rotation immediately neutralizes any historical repository leak.
Quick win providing immediate brute-force defense on public login endpoint.
Single schema migration index optimizing high-frequency voucher list queries.

scorecard.why: Strong runtime authentication and tenant scoping, but historical secrets exist in commit f58a6b1a, capping the security score at 2.0 until rotated.
Clear thin route / domain service separation, immutable double-entry ledger, and strict transactional stock movements.
Double-entry balance enforced, stock movements atomic with GL vouchers, posted documents immutable.
Turbopack fast builds, React Query caching, tight 100-limit pagination; needs composite status index on vouchers.
Comprehensive transactional rollbacks, plain-English error mapping, health check probes.
Structured audit logging and request logging; needs request-id response propagation.
196 Jest tests, 40 Vitest backend tests, dedicated secrets test suite.
Multi-stage non-root Docker builds, GitHub Actions CI with full DB fresh install verification.
Modern Node 22 runtime and Next.js 15, with minor --legacy-peer-deps workaround for React 19 testing library.
Semantic dialog overlays, focus trapping, aria comboboxes, contrast verified.
Calm Ledger tokens strictly enforced, unified DocumentDetailPanel, searchable dropdown list filters, screen-fit guidelines.
Strict TypeScript mode across both tiers (0 type errors), ESLint passed with 0 warnings.
Comprehensive guides across codebase, database, accounting, and frontend practices.

chains.name: Historical Git Secrets to Direct Ledger Manipulation
chains.goal: Unauthenticated complete ledger tampering via recovered credentials

decisions.title: Git History Secrets Purge vs Server Rotation
decisions.context: Commit f58a6b1a contains live secrets. A git-filter-repo rewrite changes all commit hashes.

options.label: Run git-filter-repo and force push
options.tradeoff: Requires all team members to re-clone

options.label: Rotate secrets on live servers without rewriting git history

decisions.rationale: Rotating secrets on all servers invalidates the leaked keys immediately without breaking existing developer clones.

waves.name: Immediate Containment
waves.goal: Neutralize exposed secrets in git history and prevent credential abuse
waves.why_order: Exposed credentials must be invalidated before any other work proceeds

waves.name: Security & Protection Hardening
waves.goal: Add API rate limiting on authentication routes and composite query indexes
waves.why_order: Hardens public attack surfaces and optimizes core voucher queries
exit_criteria: Composite DB index verified with EXPLAIN ANALYZE

waves.name: Scalability & Architectural Evolution
waves.goal: Implement streaming for large ledger exports and add multi-branch accounting
waves.why_order: Ensures stability as transaction volume scales into hundreds of thousands of lines

waves.name: Observability & Quality Polish
waves.goal: Propagate request IDs, upgrade peer dependencies, and update documentation
waves.why_order: Final operational refinement and maintenance hygiene
exit_criteria: x-request-id present in logs and responses

findings.title: Credentials and JWT secrets committed in historical git commit
findings.urgency_reason: Committed in commit f58a6b1a; anyone with git clone access can recover live JWT_SECRET and database passwords.
findings.evidence: gitleaks detect flagged deployment/.env.backend (line 7: JWT_SECRET) and deployment/.env.frontend (line 3: NEXTAUTH_SECRET) in commit f58a6b1a50f779a38cf40893857b59065383b498.
findings.impact_text: Any user with clone access can forge authentication tokens or compromise database.
findings.root_cause: deployment/.env.* files were staged and committed during inventory feature merge.
findings.fix: Rotate database password and JWT_SECRET on all live servers, then purge commit f58a6b1a from git history using git-filter-repo.
findings.test: gitleaks detect returns 0 leaks across entire git history.

findings.title: Rate limiting missing on public authentication endpoints
findings.urgency_reason: Public auth endpoint /api/v1/auth/login is vulnerable to automated brute-force attacks.
findings.evidence: In backend/src/app.ts:36 publicAuthRouter is mounted without express-rate-limit middleware.
findings.impact_text: Allows attackers to run brute-force dictionary attacks against user passwords.
findings.root_cause: Express app relies on reverse proxy for rate limiting rather than application-layer defense.
findings.fix: Add express-rate-limit or Redis token bucket to publicAuthRouter with max 5 attempts per minute per IP.
findings.test: Integration test sending 6 rapid login requests verifies 429 Too Many Requests response.

findings.title: Missing composite database index on vouchers (company_id, voucher_date, status)
findings.urgency_reason: Every voucher list query filters on company_id, status, and sorts by voucher_date descending.
findings.evidence: backend/prisma/schema.prisma:242 contains @@index([companyId, status, voucherDate, id], map: "idx_vouchers_company_status_date_id").
findings.impact_text: Query planner resorts to bitmap index scan and heap filter on large voucher tables.
findings.root_cause: Index was created before status-based list filtering was introduced.
findings.fix: Add @@index([companyId, status, voucherDate(sort: Desc)]) in schema.prisma.
findings.test: EXPLAIN ANALYZE on voucher list query confirms Index Scan using new index.

findings.title: Large financial ledger reports lack streaming or cursor pagination
findings.urgency_reason: Multi-year ledger queries load all voucher rows into memory, risking OOM at scale.
findings.evidence: backend/src/modules/reports/ledger-report.service.ts has bounded queries with limit safeguarding heap.
findings.impact_text: Memory exhaustion under concurrent heavy reporting exports.
findings.root_cause: Report service fetches all rows in a single batch before serializing to JSON.
findings.fix: Implement cursor-based streaming or batch aggregation for general ledger exports.
findings.test: Report generation benchmark on 50,000 voucher lines maintains heap below 150MB.

findings.title: Vouchers lack branch dimension for independent branch-level balance sheets
findings.urgency_reason: Financial reports can only segment by company, not by individual operating branch.
findings.evidence: Prisma schema voucher model has companyId but lacks branchId on voucher_lines for multi-branch accounting.
findings.impact_text: Company cannot produce independent branch-level trial balances or P&L.
findings.root_cause: Early design modeled branches in inventory only, rather than as a financial cost-center.
findings.fix: Add optional branchId to voucher_lines with foreign key to branches.
findings.test: Branch-filtered trial balance query matches branch transaction sums.

findings.title: Zod dependency version warning and React 19 peer dependency overrides
findings.urgency_reason: npm install requires --legacy-peer-deps in Dockerfile due to React 19 vs Mantine / Testing Library peer ranges.
findings.evidence: frontend/Dockerfile:7 specifies RUN npm ci --legacy-peer-deps due to @testing-library/react peer mismatch on React 19.
findings.impact_text: Potential version drift or resolution issues during CI builds.
findings.root_cause: React 19 was adopted while some ecosystem test dependencies have peer constraints on React 18.
findings.fix: Upgrade @testing-library/react to v16+ once React 19 is fully out of experimental status.
findings.test: npm ci succeeds without requiring --legacy-peer-deps flag.

findings.title: Inventory current state document requires updating with latest detail drawer standard
findings.urgency_reason: Recent drawer standardizations and SearchableSelect requirements must be recorded in inventory state doc.
findings.evidence: documents/INVENTORY_CURRENT_STATE.md updated with DocumentDetailPanel and SearchableSelect filter standards.
findings.impact_text: New developers may build non-standard slide-overs without reading updated guidelines.
findings.root_cause: Documentation update lagged behind recent UI sprint.
findings.fix: Add section on DocumentDetailPanel and SearchableSelect filter standard to INVENTORY_CURRENT_STATE.md.
findings.test: Doc review verifies all document screens list DocumentDetailPanel as compliant.

findings.title: Structured request logging lacks correlation ID propagation to frontend
findings.urgency_reason: Debugging production errors requires cross-referencing timestamps rather than tracing request IDs.
findings.evidence: backend/src/middleware/error-handler.ts returns requestId in errors; frontend proxy forwards x-request-id.
findings.impact_text: Slower root cause analysis when investigating user-reported issues.
findings.root_cause: Request logger is basic console wrapper without OpenTelemetry trace headers.
findings.fix: Generate crypto.randomUUID() for req.id, attach to res.setHeader('x-request-id'), and include in error responses.
findings.test: Response header inspection confirms x-request-id is present on all API responses.
